newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks fade at close ahead of US job data.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks fade at close ahead of US job data.

text.p: Australian shares finished weaker on Friday ahead of a key U.S. payrolls report later on Friday and after a choppy session which saw the All Ordinaries index trade in 20 point range around Thursday's close.
The key index closed 10.8 points lower at 2,339.4 after touching an intra-day high of 2,357.1.
Turnover was healthy and aided by see-sawing trade which fed the derivatives market. The market was directionless for much of the session and blue chips were widely mixed, dealers said.
"The gold and bank sectors held the market back for much of the session but there was some good support for some of the big resource issues after lunch," said a Sydney dealer.
The dealer said a combination of profit-taking and position squaring dragged stocks lower late in the session, with key resource companies BHP and CRA ending well off their highs.

"Wall Street could go either way tonight, but regardless of this, I think the important focus for the market next week will be local interest rates, especially after the Reserve Bank board meeting next Tuesday and of course the fluctuations of base metal prices on the LME," the dealer said.

Apart from golds, driven lower by a bullion price fall, and major banks, which were hit by profit-taking, the main interest was the debut of Orogen Minerals, the holding company of Papua New Guinea's Mineral Resources Development Corp.
After getting off to a slow start, Orogen finished the day at A$2.12 (US$1.67), a six percent premium to the institutional offer price of A$2.00.
